newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX seen settled in narrow but higher range.
newsitem.headline: German DAX seen settled in narrow but higher range.

text.p: German shares were expected to remain well-established within the tight trading range achieved after last Friday's rally, with current volumes not strong enough to push the DAX index further upwards.

With U.S. July consumer credit figures on Tuesday likely to be the only scheduled indicators to provide any new focus for the market, dealers saw the DAX index little changed from its current 2,548.73 close over the next couple of days.
"It's likely to be stable with volumes very limited," said one dealer, noting that no new direction for the market had emerged since Friday's U.S. jobs data, which sparked the rally.
The market mood in the meantime is expected to be dictated by the dollar and Wall Street, with the Dow Jones index seen moving upwards in early trade on Monday.
The U.S. currency was trading just above a support level seen at 1.4900 to the mark by mid-afternoon in Frankfurt, slightly higher than levels reached last week.
Trading in individual stocks was limited but generally higher, with the iron and steel sector, chemicals and electronics all outperforming the index.
Lufthansa AG, up 1.10 marks up at 207, was seen showing a strong rebound after heavy selling last week.
